podcast.body: The band's fifth studio album, released in 2008, marked their first collaboration with an outside producer, Danger Mouse. Danger Mouse initially had a prior commitment to produce an album for Ike Turner, but that project fell through, making him available. The album was recorded at Summa studio in Painsville, Ohio. Danger Mouse contributed as a musician, primarily playing keyboards and bass, with additional musicians providing guitars, vocals, and clarinets. Patrick Carney's drum sound on this album, influenced by a "John Bonham phase" in the summer of 2007, featured his kit set up like Bonzo's, resulting in a notably "bigger, deeper, tighter sound." "From Attack and Release, that's the album, this is called I Got Mine."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The fifth studio album, marking the band's transition to a professional studio (Summa in Painsville, Ohio) and their first collaboration with an outside producer, Danger Mouse. Danger Mouse was initially unavailable due to a commitment to Ike Turner but became available when that project fell through; he played keyboards and bass on the album, with other musicians contributing guitars, vocals, and clarinets. Patrick Carney adopted a John Bonham-inspired drum setup for this album in the summer of 2007, resulting in a bigger, deeper, tighter drum sound. "From Attack and Release, that's the album, this is called I Got Mine."
